context: Two separable decisions. (1) Wording, cheap: qualify the docs so 'salted' is stated only when machine_id_salt is configured, and say plainly that the default is deterministic and confirmable. (2) Substance, needs a call: whether the project should mint and persist a real default salt. A per-installation random salt breaks cross-installation correlation but also breaks cross-submitter grouping, which is the feature the Explorer wants; a single project-wide secret salt preserves grouping and resists offline confirmation but must be held somewhere and rotating it requires re-deriving the corpus. Record whichever is chosen as an ADR rather than leaving it implicit.
description: Codex P2 on PR #1528, but the privacy consequence is larger than the doc wording. AnonymizationConfig.machine_id_salt defaults to None and _hash_public_identifier coerces that to the empty string, so with the default ResultExporter every public pseudonym is sha256('|prefix|value')[:12] with NO secret input. That is globally deterministic and offline-computable: anyone can confirm a guessed value - a hostname, a username-bearing path, a database or bucket name - by hashing it, and can dictionary-attack the small space of common values. It does not permit enumeration, but it does permit CONFIRMATION, which is exactly what a pseudonym is supposed to prevent for a targeted subject. The entire curated corpus (207 bundles, now public on published-results) was produced with the default empty salt. Documentation added in #1528 describes the scheme as 'salted SHA-256' without the condition, which overclaims resistance to cross-installation correlation. Related: the #1512 pass-through is checked before the salt is applied, so already-anonymized values are salt-independent - see the Salt rotation section of docs/reference/result-formats.md and [[rederive-corpus-to-single-pass]].
